q: A pensioner who had opted for the Unified Pension Scheme was drawing an assured payout of Rs 40,000 per month. On his death, the family payout admissible to his spouse, at 60 per cent of the assured payout, will be:

options.A: Rs 20,000 per month
options.B: Rs 24,000 per month
options.C: Rs 30,000 per month
options.D: Rs 40,000 per month

e: UPS family payout on death of the pensioner is 60 per cent of the assured payout payable to the spouse. 60 per cent of Rs 40,000 is Rs 24,000 per month.

q: A railway pensioner drawing a basic pension of Rs 46,000 per month commutes the maximum permissible 40 per cent of his pension. The monthly amount of pension surrendered by him for commutation will be:
e: Commutation is permissible up to a maximum of 40 per cent of pension under the Commutation Rules. 40 per cent of Rs 46,000 is Rs 18,400 surrendered per month.

q: A railway servant retires with 200 days of Leave on Average Pay at his credit. His pay plus Dearness Allowance at retirement is Rs 93,000 per month. The cash equivalent of leave salary payable to him, at one-thirtieth of the monthly amount for each day of leave encashed, will be:
e: Cash equivalent is days of LAP x monthly pay plus DA divided by 30. Rs 93,000 divided by 30 is Rs 3,100 per day; for 200 days it is Rs 6,20,000.

q: A railway servant covered under the National Pension System draws basic pay of Rs 56,000 per month and Dearness Allowance of Rs 28,000 per month. The total amount credited to his Tier-I account every month, comprising his own contribution of 10 per cent and the Government contribution of 14 per cent of basic pay plus Dearness Allowance, will be:
e: NPS contributions are on pay plus DA of Rs 84,000. Employee 10 per cent is Rs 8,400 and Government 14 per cent is Rs 11,760, totalling Rs 20,160 per month.

q: A railway servant retires after completing 24 years of qualifying service, that is, 48 completed six-monthly periods. His emoluments at retirement are Rs 72,000 per month. The retirement gratuity payable to him, at one-fourth of a month's emoluments for each completed six-monthly period, will be:
e: Retirement gratuity is one-fourth of emoluments per completed six-monthly period. Rs 72,000 divided by 4 is Rs 18,000; for 48 periods it is Rs 8,64,000.

q: The last pay drawn by a deceased railway servant was Rs 74,000 per month. The family pension payable to his family at the normal rate of 30 per cent of the last pay drawn will be:

options.A: Rs 14,800 per month
options.B: Rs 18,500 per month
options.C: Rs 22,200 per month
options.D: Rs 37,000 per month

e: Family pension at the normal rate is 30 per cent of last pay drawn under the Pension Rules. 30 per cent of Rs 74,000 is Rs 22,200 per month.

q: A railway servant dies while in service after completing 12 years of qualifying service. His emoluments at the time of death are Rs 66,000 per month. The death gratuity payable to his family, at 12 times his emoluments for this length of service, will be:
e: Death gratuity for service of 5 years or more but less than 20 years is 12 times emoluments under the Pension Rules slab. 12 x Rs 66,000 is Rs 7,92,000.

q: The basic pension of a railway pensioner is Rs 38,000 per month. On his attaining the age of 95 years, the additional quantum of pension admissible to him, at 50 per cent of his basic pension, will be:

options.A: Rs 7,600 per month
options.B: Rs 11,400 per month
options.C: Rs 15,200 per month
options.D: Rs 19,000 per month

e: Additional quantum of pension at 95 years is 50 per cent of basic pension under the Pension Rules table. 50 per cent of Rs 38,000 is Rs 19,000 per month.

q: In a departmental inquiry, the Inquiring Authority records its findings and submits its report to the disciplinary authority, who proposes to impose a penalty on the charged railway servant. Before the penalty is imposed, the charged railway servant is entitled to:

options.A: A personal hearing before the Railway Board in every case
options.B: Be supplied with a copy of the inquiry report and given an opportunity to make a representation against it
options.C: Cross-examine the Inquiring Authority
options.D: Demand that the inquiry be held afresh by a different authority as of right

e: Under the Discipline and Appeal Rules, a copy of the inquiry report must be supplied to the charged servant, who gets an opportunity to represent against it before penalty is imposed.

q: A disciplinary authority proposes to punish a railway servant by withholding his privilege passes for a specified period. This penalty, under the Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, is classified as:

options.A: A major penalty
options.B: Not a penalty at all
options.C: A minor penalty
options.D: A penalty that can be imposed only by the Railway Board

e: Withholding of privilege passes or privilege ticket orders is listed among the minor penalties in Rule 6 of the Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, 1968.

q: Disciplinary proceedings are proposed against two railway servants who are jointly concerned in the same incident of alleged misconduct. In such a case, the competent authority may:

options.A: Order common proceedings against both the railway servants
options.B: Never proceed against them in the same proceedings
options.C: Proceed only against the senior of the two
options.D: Refer the matter straight to a criminal court without any inquiry

e: Rule 13 of the Discipline and Appeal Rules permits common proceedings where two or more railway servants are jointly concerned in the same case of alleged misconduct.

q: A complaint of sexual harassment at the workplace is received against a railway servant. Under the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966, such conduct on his part is treated as:

options.A: A matter outside the scope of the Conduct Rules
options.B: Permissible if it occurs outside office hours
options.C: Punishable only under the criminal law, and not departmentally
options.D: Misconduct under the Conduct Rules, rendering him liable to disciplinary action

e: Rule 3C of the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966 prohibits sexual harassment of women at the workplace and treats it as misconduct liable to disciplinary action.

q: A railway servant reports for duty under the influence of an intoxicating drink and is found unfit to perform his duties safely. His conduct is in breach of the provision of the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966 which provides that a railway servant shall:

options.A: Not absent himself from duty without leave
options.B: Not be under the influence of any intoxicating drink or drug while on duty, and take care that his performance of duty is not affected by such influence at any time
options.C: Not accept any gift from a person having official dealings with him
options.D: Not bring any political influence to bear upon his service matters

e: Rule 3B / the conduct provision on intoxicants requires that a railway servant shall not be under the influence of any intoxicating drink or drug while on duty, nor let duty be affected by it.

q: A railway servant's son is employed in a private firm which has regular official dealings with the office in which the railway servant himself is posted. In regard to such employment of a near relative, the Conduct Rules require the railway servant to:

options.A: Resign from service immediately
options.B: Conceal the employment from his office
options.C: Bring the fact to the notice of the competent authority and obtain its permission where the rules so require
options.D: Transfer his son to another firm at his own cost

e: Under the Conduct Rules, employment of a near relative in a firm having official dealings with his office must be brought to the notice of the competent authority and permission obtained where required.

q: A railway servant, to whom a railway quarter has been allotted, sublets a portion of the quarter to an outsider for rent without any permission. Such subletting of Government accommodation by him is:

options.A: Prohibited, and renders him liable to disciplinary action and cancellation of the allotment
options.B: Permitted, if the rent charged is nominal
options.C: Permitted, if the outsider is his relative
options.D: Permitted after he completes ten years of service

e: Subletting of Government accommodation without permission is prohibited under the Conduct Rules and allotment rules; it invites disciplinary action and cancellation of the allotment.

q: A railway servant is medically decategorised and a suitable alternative post for his absorption is not immediately available. Pending his absorption in an alternative post, he is ordinarily accommodated against:

options.A: A post in a lower grade in another department
options.B: Leave without pay for the entire period
options.C: A post created in a different cadre permanently
options.D: A supernumerary post created for the purpose, so that his pay is protected during the intervening period

e: A medically decategorised servant awaiting alternative absorption is accommodated against a supernumerary post created for the purpose, so his pay is protected in the intervening period.

q: An applicant under the Right to Information Act, 2005 seeks information which concerns the life and liberty of a person. Such information is required to be provided within:

options.A: 30 days of the receipt of the request
options.B: 48 hours of the receipt of the request
options.C: 7 days of the receipt of the request
options.D: 15 days of the receipt of the request

e: Section 7(5) of the RTI Act, 2005 requires information concerning the life or liberty of a person to be provided within 48 hours of receipt of the request.

q: An applicant under the Right to Information Act, 2005 is aggrieved by the decision of the Central Public Information Officer and wishes to prefer the first appeal to the prescribed appellate authority. The first appeal is ordinarily to be preferred within:

options.A: 60 days from the date of the decision
options.B: 90 days from the date of the decision
options.C: 45 days from the date of the decision
options.D: 30 days from the date of the decision

e: Section 19(1) of the RTI Act, 2005 prescribes that the first appeal against a CPIO decision is ordinarily to be preferred within 30 days from the date of the decision.

q: An ex-serviceman is re-employed on the Railways after his release from the armed forces and later retires from railway service. In regard to counting of his past military service for civil pension, the correct position is that:

options.A: His military service can be counted towards civil pension on the prescribed conditions, including refund of the pensionary benefits already drawn for that service where so required
options.B: Military service can never be counted for civil pension
options.C: Military service is counted automatically in full, without any condition
options.D: Only the war service portion of his military service can be counted

e: Past military service of a re-employed ex-serviceman can count towards civil pension on prescribed conditions, including refund of pensionary benefits already drawn for that service where required.

q: A railway servant, on expiry of the leave sanctioned to him, neither resumes duty nor obtains an extension of leave, and remains absent without any authority. Such overstayal of leave and unauthorised absence is liable to be treated as:

options.A: A period of duty for all purposes
options.B: Casual leave due to him
options.C: Leave on Average Pay, whether due or not
options.D: Dies non, with no pay for the period and a break in service unless it is condoned or regularised by the competent authority

e: Overstayal of leave and unauthorised absence is treated as dies non under the leave rules: no pay for the period, and a break in service unless condoned or regularised.

q: A railway servant had exercised an option for fixation of his pay on promotion from the date of his next increment in the lower post. On a subsequent change in the circumstances prescribed in the rules, such as a further promotion, he seeks to revise that option. In regard to such revision, the correct position is that:

options.A: An option once exercised can never be revised in any circumstances
options.B: A change of option is permissible in the circumstances and within the time allowed under the rules, such as on a subsequent promotion or reversion
options.C: The option can be revised at any time before retirement, without any condition
options.D: The option can be revised only with the approval of the Railway Board in every case

e: Pay fixation option under FR 22 can be revised in the circumstances allowed by the rules, such as on subsequent promotion or reversion, within the prescribed time limit.

q: A railway servant is granted a financial upgradation under the Modified Assured Career Progression Scheme. The level to which his pay is upgraded under the scheme is:

options.A: The level of the next promotional post in his cadre hierarchy in all cases
options.B: Two levels above his existing level
options.C: The immediate next level in the hierarchy of the Pay Matrix
options.D: The level he would have reached on completion of 30 years of service

e: MACPS grants financial upgradation only to the immediate next level in the hierarchy of the Pay Matrix, not necessarily to the level of the next promotional post in the cadre.

q: A railway servant is lent on foreign service to an organisation outside the Railways. During the period of his foreign service, his pay is ordinarily drawn from:

options.A: The foreign employer with whom he is serving
options.B: The railway revenues, as if he had continued on railway duty
options.C: The Staff Benefit Fund
options.D: His Provident Fund account

e: On foreign service, the servant's pay is ordinarily drawn from the foreign employer he is serving, who also bears the prescribed contributions, not from railway revenues.

q: A serving railway servant in a non-gazetted grade claims privilege passes for journeys with his family during a calendar year. The number of sets of privilege passes ordinarily admissible to him in a calendar year is:

options.A: One set
options.B: Three sets
options.C: Two sets
options.D: Six sets

e: A serving non-gazetted railway servant is ordinarily admissible three sets of privilege passes in a calendar year under the Pass Rules, subject to service conditions.

q: A railway servant is hospitalised for an injury sustained in the course of his duty and is granted Work Related Illness and Injury Leave for the period of hospitalisation. In regard to the debit of this leave, the correct position is that:

options.A: It is debited to his Leave on Average Pay account
options.B: It is debited to his Leave on Half Average Pay account
options.C: It is treated as Extra Ordinary Leave without any leave salary
options.D: It is a special kind of leave which is not debited to his ordinary leave account

e: Work Related Illness and Injury Leave is a special kind of leave under the leave rules and is not debited to the Leave on Average Pay or Half Average Pay account.

q: A railway servant is required to attend a court of law in the capacity of a juror or an assessor. The period of his attendance in the court is regularised by the grant of:

options.A: Leave on Average Pay debited to his leave account
options.B: Special Casual Leave for the period of such attendance
options.C: Extra Ordinary Leave without any leave salary
options.D: Duty leave only where the court issues a summons in his official capacity

e: Attendance in court as a juror or assessor is regularised by grant of Special Casual Leave for the period of attendance under the leave instructions.

q: Under the Pensions Act, 1871, a pension granted by the Government to a retired railway servant stands protected in that:

options.A: It cannot be assigned, transferred or attached, and no claim against it can be entertained by a process of any court
options.B: It can be attached by a court in execution of a decree for maintenance only
options.C: It can be freely assigned by the pensioner to a third party for valuable consideration
options.D: It is liable to attachment only after the expiry of ten years from its commencement

e: Section 4 of the Pensions Act, 1871 protects pension: it cannot be assigned, transferred or attached, and no claim against it can be entertained by process of any court.

q: A railway servant covered under the National Pension System draws basic pay of Rs 58,000 per month and Dearness Allowance at 50 per cent of the basic pay. The monthly contribution payable by the Government to his Tier-I account, at 14 per cent of basic pay plus Dearness Allowance, will be:
e: Government NPS contribution is 14 per cent of pay plus DA. Pay Rs 58,000 plus DA Rs 29,000 is Rs 87,000; 14 per cent of that is Rs 12,180 per month.

q: The lien of a railway servant on a permanent post held by him substantively comes to an end when he:

options.A: Proceeds on leave for a period exceeding one year
options.B: Is placed under suspension by the competent authority
options.C: Is granted Extra Ordinary Leave on medical certificate
options.D: Is appointed substantively to another permanent post and acquires a lien on that post

e: Lien on a permanent post terminates when the servant is appointed substantively to another permanent post and acquires a lien on that new post, under the lien rules.

q: A railway servant gives private tuition to students for remuneration in his spare time, without obtaining any sanction. Under the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966, his action is objectionable because private tuition amounts to:

options.A: Private trade or employment, which cannot be engaged in without the previous sanction of the competent authority
options.B: A political activity prohibited for all railway servants
options.C: An act of canvassing in a service matter
options.D: Acceptance of a fee from a source outside the Government revenues

e: Private tuition for remuneration is private trade or employment under Rule 15 of the Conduct Rules and cannot be engaged in without previous sanction of the competent authority.

q: The pension of a railway pensioner who retired before 01.01.2016 is revised under the 7th CPC dispensation by the method of notional fixation of pay, under which:

options.A: His existing pension is simply multiplied by the fitment factor of 2.57 in all cases, with no reference to his notional pay
options.B: His pay is fixed notionally in the pay matrix on the basis of the pay in force at each successive Pay Commission stage, and pension is worked out at 50 per cent of the notional pay so arrived at
options.C: His pension is refixed at the minimum of the level corresponding to his pre-retirement post
options.D: His pension is revised only if he applies for commutation afresh

e: Under the 7th CPC notional fixation method, pay is fixed notionally at each Pay Commission stage in the matrix and pension is worked out at 50 per cent of that notional pay.

q: Tough Location Allowance, which was earlier admissible to railway servants posted in tough location areas, stands dealt with under the 7th CPC dispensation in the manner that:

options.A: It continues to be paid as a separate allowance at the old rates
options.B: It is paid at double the earlier rates in all tough locations
options.C: It has been subsumed in the Risk and Hardship Matrix and is paid through the cell prescribed for the level of hardship
options.D: It has been merged with House Rent Allowance payable at the place of posting

e: Under the 7th CPC, Tough Location Allowance has been subsumed in the Risk and Hardship Matrix and is paid through the cell prescribed for the applicable level of hardship.

q: Licence fee recoverable from a railway servant for the railway residential accommodation allotted to him is charged:

options.A: At 10 per cent of his basic pay in all cases
options.B: At a percentage of his basic pay varying with his pay level
options.C: Only when his basic pay exceeds a prescribed ceiling
options.D: At prescribed flat rates, fixed with reference to the type and plinth area of the accommodation, and not as a percentage of his pay

e: Licence fee for railway residential accommodation is charged at prescribed flat rates fixed with reference to the type and plinth area of the quarter, not as a percentage of pay.

q: A railway servant applies for a Motor Cycle/Scooter Advance for purchase of a scooter for his personal use. Under the 7th CPC dispensation, the correct position is that:

options.A: The advance stands abolished, as all interest-bearing advances other than House Building Advance and Personal Computer Advance have been discontinued
options.B: The advance is admissible up to a maximum of Rs 20,000 only
options.C: The advance is admissible only to railway servants posted in field duties
options.D: The advance has been converted into an interest-free advance

e: Under the 7th CPC dispensation, all interest-bearing advances except House Building Advance and Personal Computer Advance, including Motor Cycle/Scooter Advance, stand discontinued.

q: A railway servant retires on superannuation after completing 23 years of qualifying service, that is, 46 completed six-monthly periods. His emoluments at retirement are Rs 72,000 per month. The retirement gratuity admissible to him, at one-fourth of a month's emoluments for each completed six-monthly period, will be:
e: Retirement gratuity is one-fourth of emoluments per completed six-monthly period. Rs 72,000 divided by 4 is Rs 18,000; for 46 periods it is Rs 8,28,000.

q: A gazetted railway servant is required by his controlling officer to attend office and perform duty on a closed holiday. In lieu of the duty so performed, he is entitled to:

options.A: Overtime Allowance at double the ordinary rate for the hours worked
options.B: Compensatory leave, to be availed of in accordance with the prescribed conditions
options.C: An additional day of Leave on Average Pay credited to his leave account
options.D: No facility of any kind, as gazetted officers cannot be compensated for holiday duty

e: A gazetted officer required to perform duty on a closed holiday is compensated by grant of compensatory leave under the prescribed conditions, not by overtime allowance.

q: A railway servant proceeding on leave is required, in regard to his address during the period of leave, to:

options.A: Surrender his residential address to the office and reside only at his home town
options.B: Obtain the permission of the Railway Board before changing his place of stay
options.C: Reside only at the station where his headquarters are situated
options.D: Intimate to the leave sanctioning authority the address at which he can be contacted during leave, and communicate any change in that address

e: The leave rules require a servant proceeding on leave to intimate the leave sanctioning authority of the address where he can be contacted during leave, and any change in it.

q: A railway servant tenders a technical resignation from his railway post in order to join another post under the Government, after applying through the proper channel and with the permission of the competent authority. In regard to his past railway service for pension purposes, the correct position is that:

options.A: His past service is counted as qualifying service in the new post, as a technical resignation does not entail forfeiture of past service
options.B: His past service is forfeited in the same manner as on an ordinary resignation
options.C: Only one-half of his past service is counted in the new post
options.D: His past service counts only if he refunds the gratuity already paid to him

e: A technical resignation to join another Government post, made through proper channel with permission, does not entail forfeiture; past service counts as qualifying service in the new post.

q: A railway servant is granted a financial upgradation under the Modified Assured Career Progression Scheme with effect from 15th March, 2026, and his pay is fixed in the higher level from the date of the upgradation itself. He will become entitled to his next annual increment in the higher level on:

options.A: 1st July, 2026
options.B: 15th March, 2027
options.C: 1st January, 2027
options.D: 1st July, 2027

e: MACPS upgradation from 15th March 2026 completes six months in the higher level before 1st January 2027, so the next annual increment falls due on 1st January 2027.

q: From the subsistence allowance payable to a railway servant under suspension, a deduction towards refund of an advance taken by him is classified as:

options.A: A compulsory deduction, which must invariably be made every month
options.B: An optional deduction, which can be made only with the written consent of the railway servant under suspension
options.C: A deduction which can be made only under an order of a court of law
options.D: A deduction which is prohibited in all circumstances during suspension

e: From subsistence allowance, refund of an advance is an optional deduction under the suspension rules and can be made only with the written consent of the suspended railway servant.

q: The last pay drawn by a deceased railway servant was Rs 84,000 per month. The family pension admissible to his family at the normal rate, being 30 per cent of the last pay drawn, will be:

options.A: Rs 16,800 per month
options.B: Rs 33,600 per month
options.C: Rs 42,000 per month
options.D: Rs 25,200 per month

e: Family pension at the normal rate is 30 per cent of last pay drawn under the Pension Rules. 30 per cent of Rs 84,000 is Rs 25,200 per month.

q: A retired railway servant who is in receipt of pension proposes to accept, after his retirement, employment under a foreign Government or an international organisation. In regard to such employment, the correct position is that:

options.A: He can accept such employment only with the previous sanction of the Government, in accordance with the pension rules
options.B: He can accept such employment freely, as the Conduct Rules cease to apply after retirement
options.C: He can accept such employment only after surrendering his pension in full
options.D: Such employment is permissible only if it is honorary and without any remuneration

e: Under the Pension Rules, a pensioner may accept employment under a foreign Government or international organisation after retirement only with the previous sanction of the Government.

q: A railway servant who is medically decategorised for the post held by him is absorbed in an alternative grade in a different cadre. His seniority in the alternative grade is reckoned:

options.A: From the date of his original appointment in the Railways
options.B: From the date of his absorption in the alternative grade, his pay being protected separately
options.C: From the date on which he was declared medically unfit
options.D: With reference to the seniority of the junior-most employee of his former grade

e: On absorption of a medically decategorised servant in an alternative grade, his seniority in that grade is reckoned from the date of absorption, his pay being protected separately.

q: In regard to the number of appointments that can be made on compassionate grounds in favour of the family of a deceased railway servant, the correct position is that:

options.A: Every eligible dependent of the deceased can be given a separate appointment
options.B: Two appointments can be made where the deceased leaves behind more than three dependents
options.C: Only one appointment on compassionate grounds can be made in favour of the family of the deceased
options.D: A second appointment becomes admissible after five years of the first appointment

e: Appointment on compassionate grounds is a one-time facility for the family: only one appointment can be made in favour of the family of the deceased railway servant.

q: A railway servant is nominated to undergo a prescribed course of training at an institution situated outside his headquarters. For the period of such training, the correct position is that:

options.A: The period of training is treated as duty, and Travelling Allowance is admissible to him as on tour for the training at the outstation
options.B: The period of training is treated as leave due and admissible to him
options.C: No Travelling Allowance is admissible, as training is a part of his normal duties at headquarters
options.D: The period of training is treated as Extra Ordinary Leave without leave salary

e: Training at an outstation institution is treated as duty, and Travelling Allowance as on tour is admissible for the training period under the travelling allowance rules.

q: A railway servant retires on superannuation with 230 days of Leave on Average Pay at his credit. His basic pay at retirement is Rs 66,000 per month and Dearness Allowance is admissible at 50 per cent of the basic pay. The cash equivalent of leave salary payable to him, worked out at the rate of pay plus Dearness Allowance for each day of leave divided by 30, will be:
e: Pay Rs 66,000 plus DA at 50 per cent is Rs 99,000 per month, or Rs 3,300 per day. For 230 days of LAP the cash equivalent is Rs 7,59,000, within the 300-day ceiling.

q: A railway servant who had opted for the Unified Pension Scheme subsequently wishes to go back to the National Pension System. The facility available to him in this regard is that:

options.A: He can switch between the two schemes any number of times during his service
options.B: A one-time, one-way switch facility from the Unified Pension Scheme to the National Pension System is available to a subscriber who had opted for the Unified Pension Scheme
options.C: No switch from the Unified Pension Scheme to the National Pension System is permissible in any circumstances
options.D: He can switch only with the permission of the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority obtained after retirement

e: UPS provides a one-time, one-way switch facility back to NPS for a subscriber who had opted for UPS; repeated switching between the schemes is not permitted.

q: A railway servant falls short of the qualifying service required for a pensionary benefit by a period of four months, the shortfall not being due to any break in service. Such a deficiency in his qualifying service may be dealt with by:

options.A: Treating the shortfall as service rendered, without any order of the competent authority
options.B: Forfeiting his entire past service for pension purposes
options.C: It cannot be dealt with by condonation, as a deficiency in qualifying service shall not be condoned under the Pension Rules
options.D: Grant of Extra Ordinary Leave for the period of the shortfall after his retirement

e: Under the Railway Services (Pension) Rules, a deficiency in qualifying service shall not be condoned. The four-month shortfall therefore cannot be made good by condonation.

q: A complaint made by a railway servant under the Public Interest Disclosure and Protection of Informers (PIDPI) Resolution is dealt with on the basis that:

options.A: The identity of the complainant is kept confidential and is not disclosed, so as to protect him from victimisation
options.B: The name of the complainant is published along with the complaint for the sake of transparency
options.C: Anonymous complaints alone are entertained under the Resolution
options.D: The complaint is required to be made only through the recognised trade union of his cadre

e: Under the PIDPI Resolution, the identity of the complainant is kept confidential and not disclosed, precisely to protect the informer from victimisation.

q: Ration Money Allowance on the Railways is an allowance admissible to:

options.A: All non-gazetted railway servants working in workshops
options.B: Railway servants who are provided with residential accommodation having no kitchen facility
options.C: Running staff for the days on which they perform running duty
options.D: Personnel of the Railway Protection Force and the Railway Protection Special Force, in lieu of the ration facilities admissible to them

e: Ration Money Allowance is admissible to personnel of the Railway Protection Force and Railway Protection Special Force in lieu of the ration facilities admissible to them.

q: A railway servant posted at a station is referred by the authorised medical officer for specialised treatment at a railway hospital situated at another station. For undertaking the journey for such treatment, the facility admissible to him is:

options.A: A privilege pass of his own entitlement, debited to his pass account
options.B: A medical pass, issued for the journey undertaken for the purpose of medical treatment on the advice of the medical authority
options.C: A duty pass, as the journey is treated as a journey on tour
options.D: No pass facility, and the journey is to be undertaken at his own expense

e: A journey undertaken on medical advice for treatment at another station is covered by a medical pass issued for that purpose under the Pass Rules, not by debit to privilege pass account.

q: The widow of a deceased person is entitled to family pension in respect of her husband's military service and also claims family pension in respect of his subsequent railway service. In regard to the two family pensions, the correct position is that:

options.A: She must elect one of the two family pensions and forgo the other
options.B: Only the higher of the two family pensions is payable to her
options.C: Family pension is admissible to her from both the sources concurrently, subject to the prescribed conditions
options.D: The railway family pension is payable only after the military family pension ceases

e: Family pension from military and railway sources can both be drawn concurrently by the widow, subject to prescribed conditions; the bar on two family pensions does not apply here.

q: It is established after the appointment of a person to a railway post that he had obtained the appointment on the strength of a false caste certificate. The consequence of such a finding is that:

options.A: His appointment is liable to be terminated, as an appointment obtained on a false certificate cannot be allowed to stand
options.B: He is allowed to continue in service, with only a recordable warning
options.C: He is merely transferred out of the vacancy reserved for his claimed category
options.D: His seniority alone is depressed to the bottom of the grade

e: Appointment obtained on a false caste certificate is void in substance and liable to be terminated when the falsity is established; such appointment cannot be allowed to stand.

q: A railway servant dies while in service after completing 12 years of qualifying service. His emoluments at the time of death are Rs 55,000 per month. The death gratuity payable to his family, at the rate of 12 times his emoluments applicable to that slab of service, will be:
e: Death gratuity for 12 years of service falls in the 5 to 20 years slab of 12 times emoluments under the Pension Rules. 12 x Rs 55,000 is Rs 6,60,000.

q: A railway servant who is an office bearer of a recognised trade union is required to attend a meeting of the executive committee of his union. The absence from duty on that account is regularised by the grant of:

options.A: Leave on Average Pay from his leave account
options.B: Special Casual Leave, admissible to office bearers of recognised unions for attending such union meetings, subject to the prescribed conditions
options.C: Extra Ordinary Leave without leave salary
options.D: Half pay leave from his Leave on Half Average Pay account

e: Office bearers of recognised trade unions are granted Special Casual Leave, subject to prescribed conditions and limits, for attending executive committee meetings of their unions.

q: A railway servant drawing basic pay of Rs 56,000 per month is posted at a station classified as a 'Z' class city for the purpose of House Rent Allowance. Dearness Allowance payable to railway servants has crossed 50 per cent, so that House Rent Allowance at that station is payable at 10 per cent of basic pay. The House Rent Allowance admissible to him will be:

options.A: Rs 4,480 per month
options.B: Rs 6,720 per month
options.C: Rs 5,600 per month
options.D: Rs 8,400 per month

e: With DA above 50 per cent, HRA rates stand revised to 30, 20 and 10 per cent; a Z class city gets 10 per cent. 10 per cent of Rs 56,000 is Rs 5,600 per month.

q: A retired railway servant residing in an area covered by the Central Government Health Scheme did not join the Retired Employees Liberalised Health Scheme at the time of his retirement. The facility open to him for medical care is that:

options.A: He may opt to join the Central Government Health Scheme by paying the prescribed contribution, in accordance with the instructions applicable to such pensioners
options.B: He is debarred for life from any Government medical facility after retirement
options.C: He can join the Retired Employees Liberalised Health Scheme at any time without paying any contribution
options.D: He is entitled only to Fixed Medical Allowance, with no facility of treatment in any hospital

e: A railway pensioner in a CGHS area who did not join RELHS may opt for CGHS by paying the prescribed contribution, under the instructions applicable to such pensioners.

q: The name of a railway servant is being considered for inclusion in a panel for promotion to a selection post. Before his promotion is ordered on the basis of that panel, it is ensured that:

options.A: He has completed at least twenty years of service in the Railways
options.B: He has not availed any leave during the preceding one year
options.C: He has passed the Appendix III departmental examination
options.D: Vigilance clearance is available in his case, that is, he is not facing any vigilance or disciplinary proceeding which stands in the way of his promotion

e: Promotion from a panel for a selection post is ordered only after vigilance clearance confirms no vigilance or disciplinary proceeding stands in the way of the servant's promotion.

q: A railway servant is compulsorily retired from service as a measure of penalty, with a balance of Leave on Average Pay standing at his credit on the date of such retirement. In regard to the cash equivalent of that leave, the correct position is that:

options.A: No leave encashment is admissible, as the retirement is by way of penalty
options.B: Cash equivalent of the Leave on Average Pay at his credit is admissible to him on such retirement, subject to the prescribed ceiling of 300 days
options.C: Encashment is admissible only for one-half of the leave at his credit
options.D: The leave at his credit is transferred to the railway servant who replaces him

e: Cash equivalent of Leave on Average Pay at credit, up to the 300-day ceiling, is admissible even on compulsory retirement by way of penalty, under the leave encashment rules.

q: A railway servant dies in harness leaving behind a son whom he had legally adopted during his lifetime. In regard to the eligibility of the adopted son for appointment on compassionate grounds, the correct position is that:

options.A: An adopted son is never treated as a dependent member of the family for this purpose
options.B: An adopted son is eligible only if the adoption took place after the death of the railway servant
options.C: A son legally adopted by the railway servant during his lifetime is treated as a dependent member of the family and can be considered for appointment on compassionate grounds, subject to the prescribed conditions
options.D: An adopted son can be considered only for a post in the lowest grade, irrespective of his qualifications

e: A son legally adopted during the railway servant's lifetime is a dependent member of the family and can be considered for compassionate appointment, subject to prescribed conditions.

q: A railway servant is granted commuted leave on medical certificate for a period of 30 days against his Leave on Half Average Pay account. The number of days to be debited to his Leave on Half Average Pay account for this spell of commuted leave will be:

options.A: 60 days
options.B: 30 days
options.C: 15 days
options.D: No debit is made, as commuted leave is a separate kind of leave

e: Commuted leave is granted against twice the amount of Leave on Half Average Pay due. Hence 30 days of commuted leave debits 60 days to the LHAP account.

q: A railway servant who has been granted leave proposes to visit a foreign country on a private visit during that leave. Before proceeding abroad, he is required to:

options.A: Surrender his railway identity card to his office for the period of the visit
options.B: Resign from service, as a serving railway servant cannot travel abroad
options.C: Obtain a no-objection from the passport authority alone, with no intimation to his office
options.D: Obtain the prior permission of, or intimate in advance, the competent authority in accordance with the instructions governing private visits abroad by railway servants

e: A serving railway servant visiting a foreign country privately during leave must obtain prior permission of, or intimate in advance, the competent authority under the governing instructions.

q: A railway servant is invited by a training institution to deliver guest lectures on a subject connected with his official work, and is offered a fee for the lectures. He can accept the engagement and the fee only:

options.A: If the lectures are delivered during his casual leave
options.B: With the previous sanction of the competent authority, as acceptance of a fee for such work requires sanction under the Conduct Rules
options.C: If the fee offered does not exceed his one month's pay
options.D: After his retirement from railway service

e: Accepting a fee for work connected with official duties, such as guest lectures, requires previous sanction under Rule 13 of the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966.

q: A gazetted railway officer claims Overtime Allowance for the hours for which he was detained in office beyond the normal working hours. His claim is liable to be rejected because:

options.A: Overtime Allowance is admissible only to running staff on the Railways
options.B: Overtime Allowance is admissible only for duty performed on Sundays and holidays
options.C: Overtime Allowance is not admissible to gazetted railway servants; it is admissible only to eligible non-gazetted staff within the prescribed ceilings
options.D: Overtime Allowance has been abolished for all categories of railway servants

e: Overtime Allowance under the Hours of Employment provisions is admissible only to eligible non-gazetted staff within prescribed ceilings; gazetted railway servants are not entitled to it.

q: A railway servant covered under the National Pension System remains on Extra Ordinary Leave without any leave salary for a period of three months. In regard to the contributions to his Tier-I account for that period, the correct position is that:

options.A: No contribution, either of the railway servant or of the Government, is made for the period for which no pay is drawn by him, as the contributions are reckoned as a percentage of the pay and Dearness Allowance drawn
options.B: The Government alone continues to pay its contribution for that period
options.C: Contributions for that period are paid out of the Staff Benefit Fund
options.D: The railway servant must pay both his own and the Government's contribution for that period in cash

e: NPS contributions are a percentage of pay and DA drawn. During Extra Ordinary Leave without pay nothing is drawn, so neither employee nor Government contribution is made for that period.

q: A railway servant is transferred from one station to another purely at his own request, the transfer not being treated as one in public interest. In regard to Composite Transfer Grant on such a transfer, the correct position is that:

options.A: It is admissible at the full rate of 80 per cent of his last basic pay
options.B: It is admissible at one-half of the normal rate
options.C: It is admissible at 33 per cent of his last basic pay
options.D: It is not admissible to him, as the transfer is at his own request and not in public interest

e: Composite Transfer Grant is admissible only on transfer in public interest. A transfer purely at the servant's own request does not attract the grant.

q: The findings of the selection committee in respect of a railway servant were kept in a sealed cover because of a pending departmental proceeding. On conclusion of the proceeding, he is completely exonerated and the sealed cover is opened, in which he is found fit for promotion. In such a case, he is entitled to:

options.A: Promotion only from the date on which a fresh vacancy arises after his exoneration, with no benefit of the panel
options.B: Promotion with effect from the date on which his immediate junior in the panel was promoted, with his seniority and notional pay fixed accordingly, arrears of pay being admissible only from the date he actually assumes the higher post
options.C: Arrears of pay of the higher post for the entire period during which the sealed cover remained unopened
options.D: Only a lump sum compensation in lieu of the promotion

e: On complete exoneration, a sealed cover selectee is promoted from the date his panel junior was promoted, with seniority and notional pay accordingly, arrears only from actual assumption.

q: A railway servant proceeds on Leave on Average Pay and remains at a station in India during the leave. The leave salary payable to him during that leave carries with it:

options.A: No Dearness Allowance, as Dearness Allowance is admissible only on duty pay
options.B: Dearness Allowance at one-half of the rate admissible on duty
options.C: Dearness Allowance at the rates in force, as a part of the leave salary admissible to him
options.D: Dearness Allowance only if the spell of leave exceeds 180 days

e: Leave salary during Leave on Average Pay within India carries Dearness Allowance at the rates in force, as a part of the leave salary admissible under the leave rules.

q: A railway pensioner wishes to have his monthly pension credited by the pension disbursing bank to a bank account which he can operate conveniently along with his wife. The facility permissible to him in this regard is that:

options.A: His pension may be credited to a joint bank account operated by him along with his spouse, as permitted under the pension payment instructions
options.B: Pension can be credited only to an account held in the single name of the pensioner
options.C: Pension can be credited to the account of his spouse alone
options.D: Pension can be credited only to a joint account held with a major son or daughter

e: Pension payment instructions permit credit of monthly pension to a joint bank account operated by the pensioner along with his spouse, as a permitted facility.

q: A railway servant dies in harness and a claim for family pension is made in respect of his children born of a marriage which was void in law. In regard to the claim of such children, the correct position is that:

options.A: The children are wholly disentitled, as the marriage itself was void
options.B: The children can claim family pension only after attaining the age of 25 years
options.C: The children are entitled only to a share of the gratuity and not to family pension
options.D: The children of a void marriage are eligible for their share of family pension in accordance with the pension rules, notwithstanding that the marriage was void

e: Children born of a void marriage are eligible for their share of family pension under the Pension Rules, notwithstanding the void status of the marriage itself.

q: A railway servant who is a member of the Territorial Army is required to attend the annual training camp of his unit during a period when he would otherwise be on duty. The period of his attendance at the camp is treated as:

options.A: Part of his Leave on Average Pay, debited to his leave account
options.B: Special Casual Leave granted for the purpose
options.C: Unauthorised absence, to be regularised later
options.D: Extra Ordinary Leave without any leave salary

e: Attendance at the annual training camp of the Territorial Army by a member railway servant is regularised by grant of Special Casual Leave for the camp period.

q: A railway servant drawing basic pay of Rs 80,000 per month is sent on deputation to another organisation at the same station. The deputation (duty) allowance admissible to him at 5 per cent of his basic pay for deputation within the same station will be:

options.A: Rs 8,000 per month
options.B: Rs 2,000 per month
options.C: Rs 4,000 per month
options.D: Rs 6,000 per month

e: Deputation (duty) allowance within the same station is 5 per cent of basic pay under the deputation rules. 5 per cent of Rs 80,000 is Rs 4,000 per month.

q: A female railway servant has already availed 365 days of Child Care Leave with full leave salary and now avails a further spell of Child Care Leave within the overall entitlement. The leave salary payable to her during this further spell is:

options.A: 80 per cent of the leave salary which would have been admissible to her
options.B: 50 per cent of the leave salary which would have been admissible to her
options.C: Full leave salary, as in the first spell
options.D: Nil, as the second spell is without leave salary

e: Child Care Leave carries full leave salary for the first 365 days and 80 per cent of leave salary for the next 365 days, so the further spell is paid at 80 per cent.

q: A female railway servant seeks Child Care Leave for the care of her child who is suffering from a disability of the prescribed degree. In such a case, Child Care Leave is admissible to her until the child attains the age of:

options.A: 18 years, as in the case of other children
options.B: 15 years only
options.C: 20 years
options.D: 22 years

e: For a child suffering from disability of the prescribed degree, Child Care Leave is admissible until the child attains 22 years of age, instead of the normal 18 years.

q: A male railway servant, who has less than two surviving children, legally adopts a child below the age of one year. In regard to paternity leave on such adoption, the correct position is that:

options.A: No paternity leave is admissible on adoption of a child
options.B: Paternity leave of 15 days is admissible to him on the adoption
options.C: Paternity leave of 30 days is admissible to him on the adoption
options.D: Only casual leave, and not paternity leave, can be granted to him

e: Paternity leave of 15 days is admissible to a male servant with less than two surviving children on legal adoption of a child below the age of one year.

q: A railway servant availing Leave Travel Concession wishes to encash Leave on Average Pay standing at his credit. He has 38 days of Leave on Average Pay at his credit, and encashment is permissible only if at least 30 days of Leave on Average Pay remain at his credit after the encashment. The maximum number of days he can encash on this occasion is:

options.A: 10 days
options.B: 38 days
options.C: 8 days
options.D: 5 days

e: LTC leave encashment is limited to 10 days at a time and to what leaves 30 days of LAP at credit. With 38 days at credit, only 8 days can be encashed on this occasion.

q: A railway servant is promoted to a higher level with effect from 20th August, 2026 and his pay is fixed from the date of his promotion itself. As he will not have completed six months of service in the higher level by 1st January, 2027, he will be entitled to his next increment on:

options.A: 1st January, 2027
options.B: 20th August, 2027
options.C: 1st January, 2028
options.D: 1st July, 2027

e: Promotion on 20th August 2026 gives less than six months in the higher level by 1st January 2027, so the next increment is deferred to the next date, 1st July 2027.

q: A railway servant has completed 10 years of regular service since his last promotion and claims a financial upgradation under the Modified Assured Career Progression Scheme. His Annual Performance Appraisal Reports for the relevant years are graded only 'Good'. The upgradation is not granted to him because:

options.A: The prescribed benchmark for grant of financial upgradation under the scheme is 'Very Good', which he does not meet
options.B: Financial upgradation under the scheme requires 20 years of service in every case
options.C: His case was not recommended by the Station Superintendent
options.D: Financial upgradations are granted only on the basis of a written examination

e: The prescribed APAR benchmark for MACPS financial upgradation is Very Good. Grading of only Good fails the benchmark, so the upgradation after 10 years is not granted.

q: A railway servant retires on superannuation while occupying a railway quarter. The retention of the quarter permissible to him after retirement is:

options.A: Two months on normal licence fee only, and no further retention in any case
options.B: Four months on normal licence fee, and a further four months on double licence fee on prescribed grounds such as education of children or medical treatment
options.C: Twelve months on normal licence fee in all cases
options.D: Retention only on payment of market rent from the date of retirement

e: After retirement, a railway quarter may be retained for 4 months on normal licence fee and a further 4 months on double licence fee on prescribed grounds like education or medical treatment.

q: A railway servant is allotted a railway quarter at his station of posting but declines to occupy it, and continues to live in a private rented house, claiming House Rent Allowance. His claim for House Rent Allowance is:

options.A: Admissible at the full rate for the station
options.B: Admissible at half the normal rate
options.C: Not admissible, as he has refused the railway accommodation allotted to him
options.D: Admissible only if he pays the licence fee of the allotted quarter

e: House Rent Allowance is not admissible where the servant refuses railway accommodation allotted to him at his station and instead lives in a private rented house.

q: A subscriber to the General Provident Fund drawing pay of Rs 50,000 per month applies for a temporary (refundable) advance from the Fund. The balance at his credit in the Fund is Rs 4,00,000. As the advance is ordinarily limited to three months' pay or half the balance at credit, whichever is less, the maximum advance ordinarily admissible to him is:
e: GPF temporary advance is limited to three months pay or half the balance at credit, whichever is less. Three months pay is Rs 1,50,000, less than half the balance of Rs 2,00,000.

q: A railway servant is imposed the major penalty of reduction to a lower post for a specified period, and the penalty order is silent on the question of his seniority on restoration. On his restoration to the higher post after expiry of the penalty period, the correct position is that:

options.A: He automatically regains his original seniority in the higher post in all cases
options.B: He can never be restored to the higher post
options.C: His pay on restoration is fixed at the minimum of the higher post invariably
options.D: He regains his original seniority only if the order imposing the penalty, or a subsequent order, so provides

e: On restoration after reduction to a lower post, the servant regains his original seniority only if the penalty order, or a subsequent order, so provides under the Discipline and Appeal Rules.

q: After the appeal of a railway servant against an order imposing a penalty on him has been disposed of, the remedy still open under the Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules is:

options.A: A second appeal to the next higher authority in all cases
options.B: Revision by the competent authority specified in the rules, either on his application or suo motu
options.C: A fresh departmental inquiry on the same charges as a matter of right
options.D: Direct imposition of a penalty by the appellate authority without any proceedings

e: After disposal of the appeal, revision by the competent authority specified in the Discipline and Appeal Rules, on application or suo motu, is the remedy still open to the servant.

q: In a departmental inquiry under the Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, the officer who had himself investigated the case and recorded the preliminary findings against the charged railway servant is appointed as the Inquiring Authority. Such an appointment is objectionable because:

options.A: An Inquiring Authority must always be a gazetted officer of the Accounts Department
options.B: The Inquiring Authority can be appointed only by the Railway Board
options.C: The Inquiring Authority should be a person who has not investigated the case or otherwise formed an opinion on it, so that the inquiry is fair and unbiased
options.D: The charged railway servant alone is competent to appoint the Inquiring Authority

e: Fair inquiry requires that the Inquiring Authority be unbiased; a person who investigated the case and formed preliminary findings on it should not be appointed to inquire into it.

q: A railway servant wishes to organise a collection of subscriptions from his colleagues and the public for a charitable purpose unconnected with his official duties. Under the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966, he may do so only:

options.A: After obtaining the previous sanction of the competent authority for raising such funds or subscriptions
options.B: After merely informing his immediate supervisor orally
options.C: Freely, as no sanction is required for charitable collections
options.D: After obtaining the permission of the local police authorities

e: Rule 12 of the Railway Services (Conduct) Rules, 1966 bars raising funds or subscriptions for any purpose without the previous sanction of the competent authority.

q: A Group 'A' railway pensioner accepts a commercial employment in a private company eight months after his retirement, without obtaining any sanction. Under the pension rules, such employment, being taken up within one year of retirement, required:

options.A: No sanction of any kind in any circumstances
options.B: Only an intimation to his former office after joining the employment
options.C: Sanction of the State Government in which the company is situated
options.D: The previous sanction of the Government, failing which his pension is liable to be withheld as provided in the rules

e: A Group A pensioner accepting commercial employment within one year of retirement needs previous Government sanction; without it, pension is liable to be withheld under the Pension Rules.

q: A railway pensioner drawing his pension through a bank at one station shifts his residence permanently to another city and requests that his pension be paid to him there. The correct position is that:

options.A: His pension cannot be transferred and must continue to be drawn at the original station only
options.B: He may get his pension transferred for payment through the prescribed procedure, by transfer of his pension payment documents to the new place of payment
options.C: He must surrender his pension and apply for a fresh pension at the new station
options.D: Transfer of pension is permissible only within the same district

e: Pension is transferable: on permanent change of residence the pensioner may get payment transferred through the prescribed procedure by transfer of his pension payment documents.

q: A railway pensioner has attained the age of 82 years. For the submission of his annual life certificate to the pension disbursing bank, the special facility available to pensioners of 80 years and above is that:

options.A: He is exempted from submitting a life certificate altogether
options.B: He may submit the life certificate only through a gazetted officer in person
options.C: He may submit his life certificate from 1st October onwards, instead of waiting for the month of November
options.D: He may submit the life certificate once in five years

e: Pensioners aged 80 years and above get the special facility of submitting their annual life certificate from 1st October onwards, instead of only in November.

q: A railway servant dies in service on 10th March and his widow prefers her claim for family pension three months later, in June. The family pension is payable to her:

options.A: From the day following the date of death of the railway servant, with arrears for the intervening period
options.B: Only from the date on which she preferred her claim
options.C: Only from the first day of the month following the month of her claim
options.D: Only after one year from the date of death

e: Family pension is payable from the day following the date of death of the railway servant, so a claim preferred three months later still carries arrears from that date.

q: A retired railway servant continues to occupy the railway quarter allotted to him well beyond the period of retention permissible after retirement, and licence fee for the period of unauthorised occupation remains recoverable from him. This amount can be recovered:

options.A: Only through a civil suit filed by the Railways
options.B: Only from his monthly pension, and not from any other dues
options.C: Only if he voluntarily agrees to pay it
options.D: From the Death-cum-Retirement Gratuity payable to him, which may be withheld to the extent of the Government dues recoverable from him

e: Licence fee for unauthorised retention of a railway quarter is a Government due recoverable from the Death-cum-Retirement Gratuity, which may be withheld to that extent.

q: Departmental proceedings are pending against a railway servant on the date of his retirement and a provisional pension is sanctioned to him. The amount of such provisional pension is:

options.A: 50 per cent of the pension admissible to him
options.B: Equal to the maximum pension admissible to him on the basis of the qualifying service rendered up to the date of retirement
options.C: 75 per cent of the pension admissible to him
options.D: A fixed amount of Rs 9,000 per month in all cases

e: Provisional pension during pending proceedings equals the maximum pension admissible on the qualifying service rendered up to retirement, as provided in the Pension Rules.

q: A railway servant with only six years of qualifying service is declared by the competent medical authority to be permanently incapacitated for further service of any kind and is retired on invalidation. In regard to his pensionary benefit, the correct position is that:

options.A: He gets no benefit, as he has not completed 10 years of qualifying service
options.B: He is entitled only to a refund of his Provident Fund subscription
options.C: Invalid pension is admissible to him even though his qualifying service is less than 10 years, calculated proportionately subject to the prescribed minimum pension
options.D: He must be retained in service till he completes 10 years of qualifying service

e: Invalid pension is admissible even where qualifying service is less than 10 years, calculated proportionately subject to the prescribed minimum pension, under the Pension Rules.

q: A railway servant who has opted for the Unified Pension Scheme retires on superannuation after completing 20 years of qualifying service. His average basic pay during the last 12 months of service was Rs 70,000 per month. As the full assured payout of 50 per cent of average basic pay requires 25 years of qualifying service and the payout is proportionate for shorter service, his monthly assured payout will be:
e: UPS payout for 20 years is proportionate to the full 50 per cent payable at 25 years. 50 per cent of Rs 70,000 is Rs 35,000; 20/25 of that is Rs 28,000 per month.

q: A railway servant applies for Extra Ordinary Leave in continuation of leave already availed by him, so that his continuous absence from duty on leave would exceed five years. The correct position under the leave rules is that:

options.A: Leave of any duration can be granted to him without restriction
options.B: He is entitled to continuous leave of up to ten years as a matter of right
options.C: The excess period is automatically treated as Leave on Average Pay
options.D: A railway servant is ordinarily not granted leave continuously for more than five years, and where continuous absence exceeds five years he is deemed to have resigned, unless the competent authority allows otherwise in exceptional circumstances

e: Leave is ordinarily not granted continuously for more than five years; continuous absence beyond five years is deemed resignation unless the competent authority allows otherwise exceptionally.

q: A railway servant granted study leave for a course of study finds that the study leave alone is insufficient and wishes to combine it with Leave on Average Pay due and admissible to him. The correct position is that:

options.A: Study leave can never be combined with any other kind of leave
options.B: Study leave can be combined only with casual leave
options.C: Study leave may be combined with other kinds of leave due and admissible to the railway servant, as provided in the rules
options.D: On combining the leaves, the entire period is treated as Extra Ordinary Leave

e: Study leave may be combined with other kinds of leave due and admissible to the railway servant, as expressly provided in the study leave provisions of the leave rules.

q: A railway servant belonging to a category exposed to the risk of accident or occupational disease is granted hospital leave for an illness directly attributable to his official duties. Hospital leave so granted is:

options.A: Debited to his Leave on Average Pay account
options.B: Not debited to his leave account, being granted in addition to the other leave due to him
options.C: Debited to his Leave on Half Average Pay account at double the rate
options.D: Treated as dies non for the entire period

e: Hospital leave for categories exposed to accident or occupational disease risk is granted in addition to other leave due and is not debited to the servant's leave account.

q: Nursing Allowance under the 7th CPC dispensation is admissible to:

options.A: Nursing personnel, such as staff nurses and nursing superintendents, working in railway hospitals
options.B: All Group 'C' staff working in railway offices
options.C: Running staff performing night duties in trains
options.D: Only the doctors employed in railway hospitals

e: Nursing Allowance under the 7th CPC is admissible to nursing personnel such as staff nurses and nursing superintendents working in railway hospitals.

q: Patient Care Allowance on the Railways is an allowance admissible to:

options.A: All railway servants posted in metropolitan cities
options.B: Patients admitted to railway hospitals, towards the cost of their treatment
options.C: Doctors drawing Non-Practising Allowance in railway hospitals
options.D: Eligible hospital staff, such as ward attendants and other specified non-ministerial staff, who are deployed on patient care duties in railway hospitals

e: Patient Care Allowance is admissible to eligible hospital staff such as ward attendants and other specified non-ministerial staff deployed on patient care duties in railway hospitals.

q: A railway servant is ordered to travel on duty by road between two stations which are not connected by rail. For the road journey so performed, he is entitled to:

options.A: No travelling allowance of any kind
options.B: Only the ordinary daily allowance, without anything for the journey
options.C: Mileage allowance at the prescribed rate for the road journey performed on duty
options.D: A free railway pass in lieu of the road journey

e: For a duty journey by road between stations not connected by rail, mileage allowance at the prescribed rate is admissible under the Travelling Allowance Rules.

q: A railway servant is transferred in public interest and joins the new station immediately, while his family travels and joins him at the new station four months later. In regard to the travelling allowance for the journey of his family, the correct position is that:

options.A: No travelling allowance is admissible, as the family did not travel with him
options.B: Travelling allowance is admissible for the family's journey, as it was performed within six months of the date of his transfer
options.C: Travelling allowance is admissible only if the family travels on the same day as the railway servant
options.D: Only half the travelling allowance is admissible for a belated journey of the family

e: Travelling allowance for the family's transfer journey is admissible if the journey is performed within six months of the transfer; four months is within that limit.
